description:
Create and/or replace many elements across any of the 22 types in one call.

Each entry in `items` is `{"type": <slug>, "element": <payload>}` (any other key
on an entry refuses the whole call) with the same payload shape `create_element`
takes: an `element` without an `id` CREATES a new element; one with an `id`
creates it if absent and REPLACES it whole if present: every field and extension
it leaves out is cleared (only links your key cannot see are kept). To change
some fields of an element, use `update_element`.
Items may reference each other by id, including a forward reference to a sibling
later in the list. There is NO delete: bulk_apply never removes an element.
When `atomic` is false (default), items succeed or fail independently and the
response reports each outcome; when `atomic` is true, ANY item failure rolls the
whole batch back and nothing is committed. Up to 1000 items. Requires a WRITE
API-Key. Returns the batch response verbatim: `{errors, items: [{status, id,
created_at, updated_at} | {status, id, error}, ...]}` — `errors` true means at
least one item failed (and, under `atomic`, that nothing committed). An item
that creates may carry `hidden: true` in its `element`, on the same terms as
create_element's `hidden`. An item that replaces an existing element changes
nothing with `hidden`: it never hides or unhides the element (update_element
names the routes that do).
Where an AI seat's writes are held for review (see
get_me), a seat's item that replaces an existing element is `{status: 202, id,
proposal}`: proposed, not applied.
`create_only` (off by default): true makes an item with an `id` only create, never
replace. An item whose `id` is already held is refused and nothing is written for
it; when the id is its only fault, the refusal is the one create_element gives
you for that id.
name: bulk_apply
